newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt to prepare for big capital inflows.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to prepare for big capital inflows.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak has told his government to prepare for an increase of $1.5 billion to $2.0 billion a year in capital inflow from abroad, government newspapers said on Monday.
Mubarak was speaking on Sunday at a meeting of the Egyptian side of the U.S.-Egyptian Presidents' Council, a private-sector consultative group. Government ministers also took part.
The meeting discussed the implications of the sovereign rating for Egypt announced by Standard and Poor's last week, a rating seen in Egypt as highly complimentary.

"He (Mubarak) reviewed the effects the rating would have on attracting capital and strengthening the ability of the Egyptian economy...to receive this increase and manage it efficiently. Cash inflows to Egypt after this report are expected to increase by between $1.5 billion and $2 billion a year," the papers said, quoting government spokesman Safwat el-Sherif.
Direct investment in Egypt amounted to $2.0 billion last year, on top of portfolio investment of $600 milion to $700 million, junior minister Youssef Boutros-Ghali said last month.
Foreign institutions are now investing large amounts in the Egyptian fixed-income market because of the high yields and low expectations of devaluation.
Mubarak said the inflows would require "a qualitative leap in Egyptian financial and monetary policies" but details were not given.
